findings.summary: Concurrent writers can corrupt the hash chain.
A crossing append can write beyond count or byte bounds.
Partial or empty surface coverage can be reported as complete.
Present and partial interaction stages can lack evidence.
Annotation patches can invalidate cards and admit placeholder completion evidence.
Ordered transitions do not enforce the operational meaning of states.
Regex-only control inventory is incomplete and misattributes controls.
No canonical child-branch, report-reconciliation, or task-switch checkpoint mechanism exists.
Full replay on every append and dashboard load violates bounded startup.
Dashboard counts become noncanonical after the first 200 cards.
An interrupted append has no authenticated tail recovery.
Snapshot generation is nondeterministic and publication is not fully durable.
Stable ID format, event uniqueness, and allocation are incomplete.
